1.1.2.en:
Fixed a crash: a malformed reply from the stick could stop the app entirely. It is now recognised as a corrupt frame and the connection is resynced.

New: a charge ceiling that works in EVERY battery mode, as a slider, a tile and a Flow action, written straight to the stick. Set below the current state of charge it stops a charge in about twenty seconds; until now the only way was a mode switch through the cloud, which takes roughly four minutes.

The battery mode is now read and set over Modbus, with the cloud as a fallback. Switching lands in seconds, and the mode is read on every poll instead of once per five-minute cloud refresh. A new tile shows the mode together with the battery power, marked when the value came from the cloud.

The reserved SOC is one slider per battery mode instead of a single tile. That value has its own register per mode and means opposite things in each - a discharge floor in Self-Consumption, a charge target in Force Charge - so one tile could not say which of the two you were looking at.

Errors from the sliders now reach you. They used to be swallowed, or to fail with a timeout after ten seconds even when the change had gone through.

Also: two Flow actions that cap charge or discharge power without switching the battery mode, and a Flow action for the reserved SOC of a named mode. The register scan and the values table in the app settings now cover the registers identified for this hardware.

Note: the max charge power setting only governs while the station is in Force Charge, and the max discharge power only in Force Discharge. Neither limits anything in Self-Consumption. The card hints have been corrected accordingly.

A mode you pick is now confirmed from the stick instead of the cloud. The cloud still reports the previous mode for minutes after a switch, and reading it there wrote that stale value back into the picker — so a switch that had already taken effect looked like it had fallen back. The ten-second gap between switches is also skipped when the write goes over Modbus, where there is nothing to wait for.

The reserved SOC is now written over Modbus as well, for Self-Consumption, Force Charge and Force Discharge alike. It used to go through the cloud on purpose, because the register depends on the battery mode and that mode was only known from the five-minute cloud refresh; reading it off the stick removed that risk. Modes without a known register still use the cloud. Self-Consumption turns out to have TWO floor registers and the inverter honours the higher one. The app now writes the same register the cloud uses and parks the other at zero, so the floor you set is the floor that binds; it still reads both and shows the higher, so a value set elsewhere can never hide behind a lower number on the card. Worth knowing: that register does not only block discharging, it charges the battery back up to its level — from the grid if there is no sun.
1.1.2.nl:
Crash opgelost: een misvormd antwoord van de stick kon de app volledig laten stoppen. Dit wordt nu herkend als een corrupt frame en de verbinding wordt opnieuw opgezet.

Nieuw: een laadplafond dat in ELKE batterijmodus werkt, als schuif, tegel en Flow-actie, rechtstreeks naar de stick geschreven. Zet je het onder de huidige laadtoestand, dan stopt het laden in ongeveer twintig seconden; tot nu toe kon dat alleen met een moduswissel via de cloud, en die duurt ruwweg vier minuten.

De batterijmodus wordt nu via Modbus gelezen en gezet, met de cloud als terugval. Schakelen is een kwestie van seconden, en de modus wordt bij elke poll gelezen in plaats van eens per vijf minuten uit de cloud. Een nieuwe tegel toont de modus samen met het accuvermogen, met een markering als de waarde uit de cloud kwam.

De gereserveerde SOC is een schuif per batterijmodus geworden in plaats van één tegel. Die waarde staat per modus in een eigen register en betekent per modus het tegenovergestelde - een ondergrens voor ontladen in Zelfconsumptie, een laaddoel in Force Charge - dus één tegel kon niet zeggen welke van de twee je zag.

Foutmeldingen van de schuiven komen nu bij je aan. Die werden eerder ingeslikt, of faalden na tien seconden met een timeout terwijl de wijziging wel doorging.

Verder: twee Flow-acties die het laad- of ontlaadvermogen begrenzen zonder de batterijmodus te wisselen, en een Flow-actie voor de gereserveerde SOC van een specifieke modus. De registerscan en de waardentabel in de app-instellingen dekken nu de registers die voor deze hardware zijn vastgesteld.

Let op: de instelling voor max laadvermogen geldt alleen zolang de omvormer in Force Charge staat, en max ontlaadvermogen alleen in Force Discharge. In Zelfconsumptie begrenzen ze niets. De kaarthints zijn daarop aangepast.

Een modus die je kiest wordt nu bevestigd vanaf de stick in plaats van uit de cloud. De cloud meldt na een wissel nog minutenlang de vorige modus, en die werd daar teruggelezen en zo in de keuzeschakelaar teruggezet — waardoor een wissel die allang was doorgevoerd leek terug te vallen. De wachttijd van tien seconden tussen twee wissels vervalt ook als er via Modbus geschreven wordt, want daar valt niets op te wachten.

De gereserveerde SOC wordt nu ook via Modbus geschreven, zowel voor Zelfconsumptie als Force Charge en Force Discharge. Dat ging bewust via de cloud, omdat het register van de batterijmodus afhangt en die modus alleen uit de cloudverversing van vijf minuten bekend was; door hem van de stick te lezen is dat risico weg. Modi zonder bekend register gebruiken nog steeds de cloud. Zelfconsumptie blijkt TWEE ondergrens-registers te hebben en de omvormer houdt de hoogste aan. De app schrijft nu hetzelfde register als de cloud en parkeert het andere op nul, zodat de ondergrens die je instelt ook de ondergrens is die geldt; hij leest ze nog wel allebei en toont de hoogste, zodat een waarde die elders is gezet zich nooit achter een lager getal op de kaart kan verstoppen. Goed om te weten: dat register blokkeert niet alleen het ontladen, hij laadt de accu ook actief bij tot dat niveau — uit het net als er geen zon is.

1.1.1.en: Reserve level, max charge power and max discharge power are now read straight from the DTS stick over Modbus, so they are current immediately instead of lagging the cloud by minutes, and each now also appears as its own value tile on the device card with a distinct icon. They refresh on the normal live poll, so a change made in S-Miles shows up within a minute rather than after the five-minute settings refresh, and moving a slider updates its tile straight away. Changing them goes over Modbus too where that is exactly equivalent: the reserve level always, and the two power limits when the battery is already in the matching Force Charge / Force Discharge mode — otherwise the cloud is still used, because only the cloud can switch mode as well. Every local write is confirmed by reading the register back, so a dropped write can never leave a wrong setting behind. The cloud marker is now applied per value and disappears from anything actually read locally. The reserve setting is renamed to "Reserved SOC", matching Hoymiles' own wording: it is the floor the battery discharges to in Force Discharge, but the ceiling it charges up to in Force Charge, so calling it a minimum was wrong in half the modes. There is no separate max charge level — that ceiling is this same per-mode value. The battery mode itself stays cloud-only; no register anywhere in the stick reflects it. Modbus now keeps a single connection open per stick instead of opening and closing one for every register it reads. That was the real cause of the connection resets and dropped readings the DTS-WL-G3 was blamed for: the same probe went from constant failures to 12 out of 12 clean once the connection was reused. Replies are matched to their request by transaction id, so a late answer can no longer be handed to the wrong reader — which is what used to shift every address in a register scan by one block. An unreachable stick is also handled far better: a failed connect is remembered briefly, so a full read of a stick that is off now takes 9 seconds instead of 64. The register scan retries a chunk that drops out and reports how many registers it could not read, instead of letting a gap look like an empty address range. The Values tab in the app settings now also lists the three settings that are read locally, with the register each one comes from — including the reserved SOC, which sits at a different address per battery mode and moves to the cloud list for modes that have none. The register scan now also covers the FC03 settings block, so every register the app reads or writes appears in the dump and is labelled — including the reserved SOC of each battery mode. Holding registers are prefixed FC03 because those addresses are a separate space from the input registers. Fixed: moving the max charge level slider could silently switch the whole battery to Peak Shaving. When the active mode has no max charge level, the app now says so instead of changing the mode behind your back. Battery state of charge is also checked against the previous reading, so a bad response can no longer show up as a sudden 0% — seen live going from 92% to 0% and back twenty seconds later. Battery settings live per mode, so the app no longer shows one mode's value while another is running: reserve level and max charge level are now blanked when the active mode has no such setting, instead of borrowing a number from a different mode. The charge and discharge power limits stay visible, because each names its own mode and can be prepared locally without switching to it. New: per-module cell data, read straight from the battery over Modbus — the cloud does not expose it at all. The device card gains two tiles, cell spread in mV and the highest cell temperature, refreshed every fifteen minutes so Homey builds history; a spread creeping up over months is the earliest sign of a weakening cell. All individual cell voltages and temperatures per module are available on request from the app settings, rather than being polled continuously. The module addresses are detected and then remembered, so this costs a few seconds once instead of on every start. Offline resilience: the active battery mode is now remembered on the device, so a restart while the internet is down still knows which per-mode register a local write should target. With no cloud at all the app keeps reading every live value and the cell data, and keeps setting the reserve level and the charge and discharge power limits over Modbus — enough to hold or release the battery during an outage. Switching between modes still needs the cloud; no register anywhere reflects it. The connection tab now checks whether the gateway actually serves the protocol you picked: a DTS-WL-G3 only opens port 502, so choosing the native protocol there could never work and used to fail in ways that looked like a broken setup. It now says so instead.

1.0.2.en: Added App Store and Play Store links for account creation. Improved login disclaimer clarity. Added English translations for all pairing views.

1.0.0.en: Initial release. Monitor and control your Hoymiles HiOne battery system from Homey via S-Miles Cloud or local LAN.

1.0.3.en: Rewrite S-Miles Cloud API client (v3 auth with Argon2, multi-client profiles, correct battery mode IDs) and add app settings for saved cloud login and gateway/DTS IP/port. Extend monitoring with reserve SOC, energy totals, CO2 and EPS savings sensors; add Flow actions for reserve SOC, peak shaving, relay, and local power limit/inverter control. Improve pairing with saved credentials and prefilled gateway IP, and migrate new capabilities on existing devices.

1.0.4.en: Added Modbus TCP support for the DTS-G3 stick with a register-scan diagnostic, and a 'supported battery modes' diagnostic to see which modes your system accepts. Hardened cloud login: backs off after failures (12h on lockout/wrong-account errors) to protect your S-Miles account from repeated login attempts. The device is now a Homey Home Battery: charging/discharging power and charged/discharged energy are tracked in Homey Energy. Fixed percentage sliders showing 100x too high and clarified slider labels. NOTE: existing devices must be removed and re-added to apply the new battery device type.

1.0.5.en: Gateway info (model, serial number, firmware and hardware version) now fills in on cloud-only and Modbus setups, not just over the local connection, and shows the gateway model. Serial number is now shown in decimal to match the label and the S-Miles portal. Added a LAN auto-detect scan and per-device protocol pinning (native 10081 / Modbus 502). Corrected the labels for battery modes 5 and 6 to Force Charge / Force Discharge, added mode help and a charge/discharge status, fixed the sign of the battery power reading, and split the maximum charge and discharge power into separate sliders.

1.0.6.en: Fixed the battery power reading on the cloud connection: the HiOne reports only the magnitude, so the app now derives the charge/discharge direction itself (from the live energy-flow data, the forced charge/discharge modes, the battery energy counters and the SoC trend) — charging shows as positive and discharging as negative in the power tile, the charge/discharge status and Homey Energy. The active battery mode is now also read on every data poll, so mode changes show up much sooner. Added a Connected devices overview under System info that lists every device (DTU, inverter, backup box, …) with its type, status, generation, model, serial number, firmware and hardware version in a copyable field. Added Flow condition cards 'Battery is idle' and 'Battery is discharging', and Flow action cards to set the max charge power (Force Charge) and max discharge power (Force Discharge) separately. Each mode-specific Flow action now states which battery mode it applies to. The battery mode now refreshes faster, and after a mode or power change the live data is re-read after a few seconds so the new charge/discharge state shows sooner. Percentage sliders (reserve SOC, max SOC, max charge/discharge power) are now stored as a plain 0–100 value so their Insights graphs read the real percentage instead of a value 100× too small. Selecting a battery mode is now debounced and rate-limited, so scrolling through the picker no longer applies every mode and a quick second change waits out the cloud's cooldown instead of erroring.

1.0.7.en: Redesigned the app icon: a bold battery badge with the Hoymiles H as a cutout, readable both large and at the small size shown in the app card. Fixed the icon not rendering at all in a previous test build (gradients broke Homey's icon renderer; switched to flat colors) and regenerated the driver icon files that had gone stale.

1.0.8.en: Fixed the app icon not showing on the App Store listing (it rendered as a plain green circle): reverted to the original simple lettermark design for the app-level icon, which the Store's icon renderer handles reliably. The device icon keeps the new battery badge design, since that one renders correctly.

1.0.9.en: Hardened the app against internet outages: overlapping polls and settings reads are single-flight, slider/control errors are caught, cloud login is shared and coalesced across devices, and network auth failures retry after 1 minute instead of waiting 30. Added AI Mode (battery mode 9). Live data still polls about every 60s; heavy mode/settings reads now run every 5 minutes. Local protocol defaults to Modbus TCP (Auto still available: Modbus then native 10081). Default Modbus unit ID is 1 (verified answering on DTS-WL-G3); after enabling Remote Control the installer may set 101–254. Native 10081 pauses for an hour after connection refused. Battery SoC, power and voltage now prefer verified local Modbus registers; battery current is derived from local power and voltage, while missing values still fall back to cloud.

1.1.0.en: Grid power, solar power and home load are now read locally over Modbus as well, so nearly all live values update immediately instead of lagging minutes behind the cloud. Only the battery mode, energy counters, CO2 and savings still come from S-Miles Cloud; these are marked with a small cloud symbol so you can see at a glance which values are instant. The device also shows its connection source. Modbus readings are now checked against a plausible range and retried once, so a stray 'no data' response can no longer show up as a real measurement. The app settings page is split into Account, Connection and Values tabs, where the Values tab lists every measurement with the register it comes from. The register scan now covers the windows that actually hold live data, pauses polling while it runs and completes in a few seconds instead of timing out. Also fixed: the diagnostics page lets you pick which battery to inspect when your account has more than one, and AI Mode is no longer reported as unsupported.
